glyph_origin: Unclear. Theories include: • Zhongshu Xu: Pictogram (象形): tongue sticking out from the mouth. • Meilan Chen: Ideogrammic compound (會意): abbreviated 壴 + 口, hence a decorated drum and an open mouth. Shuowen interprets it as 牛 + 口; however, Yu Xingwu points out that the top component is unrelated to 牛, as can be seen in the oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions.
shuowen: Shuowen interprets it as 牛 + 口;
senses: (Southwestern Mandarin) to try; to check out
[jū] (obsolete in standard Chinese) to interrogate and convict
